reporting-org.narrative: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria

title.narrative: Contributing to rapid and sustained scale-up of Malaria Control Interventions for Impact in Nigeria - Nigeria (01-Feb-2015-31-Dec-2017)

description.narrative: Nigeria, Malaria, National Malaria Elimination Programme of the Federal Ministry of Health of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (NMEP)This program has the following goals: To reduce malaria burden to pre-elimination levels and bring malaria-related mortality to zero by 2020. The objectives of this program are: At least 80% of health facilities in all LGAs report routinely on malaria by 2020, progress is measured, and evidence is used for programme improvement.. To ensure the timely availability of appropriate antimalarial medicines and commodities required for prevention and treatment of malaria in Nigeria wherever they are needed by 2018.. To provide adequate information to all Nigerians such that at least 80% of the populace habitually takes appropriate malaria preventive and treatment measures as necessary by 2020. To provide at least 80% of targeted population with appropriate preventive measures by 2020.. To strengthen governance and coordination of all stakeholders for effective program implementation towards an 'A’ rating by 2017 sustained through to 2020 on a standardized scorecard.. To test all care-seeking persons with suspected malaria using RDT or microscopy by 2020.. To treat all individuals with confirmed malaria seen in private or public facilities with effective anti-malarial drug by 2020

title.narrative: Impact indicators targets and results for NGA-M-NMEPP01
Modelled lives saved (based on latest epidemiological data)
Reported malaria cases (presumed and confirmed)
Malaria parasite prevalence: Proportion of children aged 6-59 months with malaria infection
In-patient malaria deaths: rate per 100,000 persons per year
Confirmed malaria cases (microscopy or RDT): rate per 1000 persons per year
Malaria test positivity rate
Outcome indicators targets and results for NGA-M-NMEPP01
Malaria O-Other 2: Percent of children with fever in the last two weeks who had blood taken from a finger or heel for testing
Malaria O-Other 1: Percent of pregnant women who received 3 or more doses of intermittent preventive treatment during antenatal care visits (in public & private facilities)
Proportion of households with at least one insecticide-treated net for every two people
Proportion of malaria cases (presumed and confirmed) that received first line antimalarial treatment at private sector sites
Malaria O-Other 3: Percent of children under 5 years of age with fever in the last 2 weeks who received any antimalarial treatment
Proportion of children under five years old who slept under an insecticide-treated net the previous night
Proportion of pregnant women who slept under an insecticide-treated net the previous night
Proportion of population with access to an ITN within their household
Coverage / Output indicators targets and results for NGA-M-NMEPP01
CM-other 5: Proportion of confirmed malaria cases that received first-line antimalarial treatment according to national policy in the community - public sector
CM-other 1 : Percentage of patients admitted for severe malaria that received injectable artesunate as treatment - public sector
CM-other 2: Proportion of suspected malaria cases that receive a parasitological test in the community - public sector
VC-other 2: Number of long-lasting insecticidal nets distributed to targeted risk groups (primarily pregnant women and children U5) through continuous distribution by the public and private sector
VC-other 1: Number of long-lasting insecticidal nets distributed to at-risk populations through mass campaigns (Global Fund specific)
Number of long-lasting insecticidal nets distributed to at-risk populations through mass campaigns
Proportion of targeted risk groups receiving long-lasting insecticidal-nets
CM-other 3 : Number of co-paid ACTs distributed through the First-Line Buyers
Proportion of pregnant women attending antenatal clinics who received three or more doses of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria
Number of long-lasting insecticidal nets distributed to targeted risk groups through continuous distribution
Proportion of health facilities without stock-outs of key commodities during the reporting period
Proportion of suspected malaria cases that receive a parasitological test at public sector health facilities
Proportion of malaria cases (presumed and confirmed) that received first line antimalarial treatment at public sector health facilities
Percentage of HMIS or other routine reporting units submitting timely reports according to national guidelines
Proportion of population at risk potentially covered by long lasting insecticidal nets distributed
Proportion of confirmed malaria cases that received first-line antimalarial treatment at public sector health facilities
